Edit: on the flip side, do you feel that buying these games rewards developers who support their games after launch?

It's not the people buying when the game improves that are supporting the "release first, finish development second" attitude, it's the people buying the broken game at launch (or even before launch). If nobody bought broken games, broken games wouldn't get published.

That being said, it depends on who is doing it. Sometimes a borked release is an accident: after all, a big release day could easily put more player-hours into a game than anyone could reasonably expect from the QA cycles during development. But a couple of big companies have made a habit of it, and they won't get my money until they show a consistent change in attitude, no matter how much post-launch improvement they wring out. That has more to do with how they treat their customers across the board, though, and less to do with broken launches. Broken launches are a symptom in that case.

Why We Should Embrace Not Fear the Biohacker Uprising

Hahahaha... The programming culture of the 70s and 80s is so vastly different, I don't even know where to begin. I think Vivek Wadhwa is right -- I think we have to be very afraid, not Shelly Fan and her "passion". And the funny thing is that for the first half of her piece she does exactly that, and then she says, essentially -- "oh but most of them are different". Yeah, but it only takes a couple to do amazing damage. In fact, it's probably just a dumb mistake, a rookie error, rather than an intentional one, that does us in...
The only one in fear of biohackers are the pharmaceutical and agricultural companies. They fear a loss of profits and loss of claiming those patents before anyone else does.

And I for one welcome our insect overlords. But on a serious note while I don't like the idea of surveillance and over-regulation, I think this should be monitored because even smart people do dumb stuff. It's possible someone may royally fuck up like making a bacteria that attacks bananas which because all bananas are the same we suddenly lose almost all bananas in the world. But on the other hand we could see something like organ regeneration coming out of this community. So while I don't think it should be gotten rid of, it should be regulated in some way. We're beginning to advance to super science, and we should tread lightly.
